L01 | Deciding which other sources could plausibly change the answer owed to the person, and when the search has gone far enough to stop.
L02 | Deciding how much evidence is enough for the use the claim will be put to, and how plainly to word the limits.
L03 | Deciding what observed behavior counts as real proof that the change is in effect, rather than merely saved.
L04 | Very little remains beyond deciding which clock and time zone are the right ones for the record at hand.
L05 | Choosing a deliberate failure that truly resembles the failure the test or monitor is meant to catch, and inducing it safely.
L06 | Deciding which lessons deserve to become permanent steps, and where in the work each step should sit so it actually fires.
L07 | Deciding when the evidence is strong enough to name a cause, and how to mark a paraphrase clearly when an exact quote is not possible.
L08 | Nearly all of it remains judgment, since recognizing a request for presence and knowing what calm attention looks like in that moment cannot be reduced to a step.
L09 | Deciding whether a source is independent enough to count as outside yourself, and whether an unchecked answer is still worth giving with its label.
L10 | Deciding how far the neighborhood of a fix extends, and which adjacent things are close enough to need checking.
L11 | Deciding, once the search is confirmed to have run fully, whether the empty or short result is strong enough to support a claim about the world.
L12 | Deciding how much testing a repeated fact deserves given the stakes, and which caveats must travel with it.
L13 | Deciding which landed outcome to inspect, and how much of it must be examined before the success report is believed.
L14 | Weighing how long to keep investigating location and reading errors before acting, especially when the recovery action is itself destructive.
L15 | Deciding which work is important enough to warrant it, and which reviewer differs in the way that matters for this kind of error.
L16 | Identifying which single check is truly the deciding one for a given piece of work.
L17 | Little remains except noticing which strings are long or important enough to require the tool, and confirming that the source being copied is the right one.
